hints: Look at what each test tells you separately, starting with 2,4-DNPH which only detects one type of functional group.
Fehling's reagent narrows it down further, as only aldehydes (not ketones) give the red-brown precipitate.
Now ask which aldehyde also contains the CH3CO group needed for a positive iodoform test with alkaline iodine.
walkthrough:
**Interpret the 2,4-DNPH result**

Q gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, so Q must contain a carbonyl group, C=O. That means Q is either an aldehyde or a ketone.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} + 2,4\text{-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Interpret the Fehling's result**

Q gives a red-brown precipitate with Fehling's reagent. Only aldehydes are oxidised by Fehling's, ketones do not react.

Test rule:
$$\text{RCHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O(s, red-brown)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So Q must be an aldehyde.

**Interpret the alkaline iodine result**

Q gives a pale yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine. This is the iodoform test for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3\text{(s, pale yellow)} + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Only a molecule that is both an aldehyde and contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ fits all three tests.

**Identify Q**

Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde and it contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ unit. It therefore gives all three positive results, so it is the identity of Q.

options.A: Ethanal, CH3CHO, is an aldehyde so it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH and is oxidised by Fehling's to give red-brown Cu2O. It also has the CH3CO group, so it gives pale yellow CHI3 with alkaline iodine. It fits all three observations.
options.B: Propan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH3, is a secondary alcohol, not a carbonyl compound, so it gives no reaction with 2,4-DNPH and no reaction with Fehling's. Students may remember it gives a positive iodoform test, but that alone is not enough.
options.C: Propanal, CH3CH2CHO, is an aldehyde so it is positive with 2,4-DNPH and Fehling's, but it does not contain the CH3CO group. It therefore gives a negative iodoform test, so it fails the third observation.
options.D: Propanone, CH3COCH3, is a ketone so it is positive with 2,4-DNPH and positive with alkaline iodine, but ketones are not oxidised by Fehling's. It fails the second observation.
